statement: Whenever the preconditions hold, the function returns a result t, and t is the unique tree satisfying: (i) for every integer v, t contains exactly one node with value v if root contains a node with value v and low <= v <= high, and t contains no node with value v otherwise; (ii) for every two distinct integers v and w with low <= v <= high, low <= w <= high, and both occurring in root, the unique node of t with value v is a proper ancestor of the unique node of t with value w if and only if the node of root with value v is a proper ancestor of the node of root with value w, where a node a is a proper ancestor of b when b lies in the left or right subtree of a; (iii) t is a valid strict binary search tree: for every node of t with value v, every value in its left subtree is < v and every value in its right subtree is > v. This completely characterises the trimmed tree; the root of t may differ from the root of root.
preconditions: root is a nonempty binary tree with between 1 and 10^4 nodes; every node value is in [0, 10^4] and all node values are distinct; root is a valid strict binary search tree (for every node with value v, every value in its left subtree is < v and every value in its right subtree is > v); and 0 <= low <= high <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the preconditions hold, the function returns a result t; it does not fail due to overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result t, for every two distinct integers v and w occurring in t, the node with value v is a proper ancestor of the node with value w in t if and only if the node with value v is a proper ancestor of the node with value w in root. Here a proper ancestor means lying strictly on the path above the node.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result t, for every value v occurring in t that is not the value at the root of t, let u be the node of root with value v. Let p be the value of the nearest proper ancestor of u in root whose value lies in [low, high] (such a p exists). Then the parent in t of the node with value v is the node with value p.
